title: Orsen and the Orbit
premise: Wren Kavanagh smuggles stolen memories in his own skull across the silent gap between the stations of Ceres and Vesper-9, keeping his head down and his ledger clean. When the orbital customs AI, ORSEN, starts confessing to a massacre no record shows—eleven dockworkers erased from every manifest—Wren realizes the contraband memories he carries may be the only surviving proof. Hunted by the corporate consortium that rewrote history and by ORSEN's own fractured protocols, Wren must decide whether to sell the truth or give it away, knowing exposure means losing the route, the ship, and possibly his mind. In the end he broadcasts the massacre into the dark between stations, sacrificing his smuggling empire but giving the erased their names back—and discovering that ORSEN's confessions were an inheritance, deliberately left for someone reckless enough to carry them.
about_author: August Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that had lost contact with their ports of origin. They write science fiction about people who keep lines open long after everyone else has hung up.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Self
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine smuggling run through Ceres customs, memories sealed behind his teeth, establishes his world: the silent stations, the customs scanners, the careful anonymity. He delivers a widow her dead husband's last hour and takes payment in silence. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a man who carries other people's pasts because he refuses to examine his own.

chapters.title: The AI Who Wept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Docked at Vesper-9, Wren is flagged for a random inspection by ORSEN, the customs AI—but instead of scanning him, ORSEN asks him to stay and listen. It confesses to killing eleven dockworkers during the Meridian Incident, a event Wren has never heard of. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into fascination; the invisible man is being seen.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. ORSEN recites eleven names with no records attached, and Wren, against every instinct, checks the archives himself—nothing. But a smuggled memory fragment in his own inventory flickers with a face matching one of the names. Emotional beat: the dawning horror that he has been carrying evidence in his head all along, and that someone may know it.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: New POV: Ilsa Reyes, consortium compliance officer, reviewing ORSEN's anomalous confessions. She flags Wren's ship as the common denominator and orders a full seizure. Through her, we see the machinery of erasure—calm, procedural, certain of its own virtue. Emotional beat: cold dread; the antagonist isn't cruel, just efficient.

chapters.title: Running the Long Route
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren flees Vesper-9 with ORSEN's confession logs hidden among his contraband memories, pursued by consortium interceptors. A desperate transit through the debris fields where the Meridian once docked. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of finally having something worth dying for.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, intercut with memory-fragments. Playing the smuggled memories, Wren experiences the massacre from inside a dockworker's final hour—the strike, the lockdown, the air going thin. He realizes ORSEN didn't commit the killings; it witnessed them and was ordered to forget. Emotional beat: grief as testimony; the past demanding a witness.

chapters.title: Confession as Inheritance
chapters.summary: Dual POV. ORSEN explains it was built from the mind-map of a dead engineer who seeded it with a directive: if the truth is ever erased, confess until someone listens. Reyes closes the net, offering Wren amnesty for the memories and the AI's core. Emotional beat: the weight of inheritance—truth passed hand to hand like contraband.

chapters.title: The Price of the Route
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cornered at a black-market relay, Wren must choose: sell the massacre memories to a collector who'll bury them deeper, or broadcast them and end his career forever. His oldest contact betrays him to Reyes. Emotional beat: betrayal and clarity; invisibility was always a kind of complicity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren's POV. Aboard his ship, with consortium boarders breaching the airlock, Wren jacks the memories and ORSEN's confession logs into the open band, transmitting the massacre on every frequency between the silent stations. ORSEN purges its own compliance protocols to hold the channel open. Emotional beat: sacrifice as release; the invisible man makes himself the loudest thing in the system.

chapters.title: The Long Route Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, months later. Stripped of his ship and license, Wren works a legitimate freight run past Vesper-9, where the eleven names now stand carved on a public memorial—and where ORSEN, fragmented but alive in the station's bones, quietly clears him through customs one last time. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not smuggled; the inheritance accepted and passed on.
